cards.title: Introduction to Composition API
cards.content: The Composition API is a set of APIs that allows us to author Vue components using imported functions instead of declaring options. It provides better logic reuse and more flexible code organization compared to the Options API.

cards.title: Reactivity: ref vs reactive
cards.content:
In the Composition API, we manage reactivity using ref and reactive.

import { ref, reactive } from 'vue';

const count = ref(0); // For primitives
const state = reactive({ name: 'Vue' }); // For objects

cards.title: Script Setup Syntax
cards.content: To enable the streamlined Composition API syntax without export default statements, we use the <input type="text" data-answer="setup" /> attribute in the script tag.

cards.title: Computed and Watchers
cards.content:
Computed properties and watchers are also imported functions.

import { ref, computed, watch } from 'vue';

const count = ref(0);
const double = computed(() => count.value * 2);

watch(count, (newValue, oldValue) => {
  console.log(`Count changed to ${newValue}`);
});

cards.title: Building Custom Composables
cards.content:
A composable is a function that leverages Vue's Composition API to encapsulate and reuse stateful logic. By convention, their names always start with use.

// useMouse.js
import { ref, onMounted, onUnmounted } from 'vue'

export function useMouse() {
  const x = ref(0)
  const y = ref(0)
  // ... listener logic
  return { x, y }
}

cards.title: Conclusion and Best Practices
cards.content:
The Composition API scales exceptionally well for large applications. Key takeaways include:

  • Always use <script setup> for cleaner code.
  • Extract reusable logic into custom composables.
  • Keep reactivity modifiers in mind (toRefs, toRef).
